answer.answer:
Two firms stand out as repeat joint-development partners across multiple robotic construction processes: Firm_060 and Firm_082. Firm_060 shows up as a manufacturer in four separate co-development cases with four different partner sets, while Firm_082 appears in two cases with two different partners. All other firms in this dataset appear in only a single joint-development record each.

**Firm_060: repeated co-development across four cases**

Firm_060 is named as a manufacturer in four distinct census cases, each time paired with a different set of partners:

- Joint development partnership: Firm_060, Firm_073, Firm_008 jointly developed this construction robot [1] (census_RXM6-11).
- Joint development partnership: Firm_060, Firm_015, Firm_062 jointly developed this construction robot [2] (census_RXM6-8).
- Joint development partnership: Firm_060, Firm_034 jointly developed this construction robot [3] (census_RXM6-16).
- Joint development partnership: Firm_060, Firm_030 jointly developed this construction robot [4] (census_RXM6-10).

Notably, one of these cases points to material use: census_RXM6-16 involves Firm_060 and Firm_034 on a process that usesMaterialNode Concrete, while census_RXM6-11 and census_RXM6-8 both connect to Material_Steel via the same "usesMaterialNode" edge. This suggests Firm_060 has co-developed processes spanning at least two different material domains (concrete and steel), though the graph only records the co-occurrence, not a directional dependency between Firm_060 and any specific material capability.

**Firm_082: repeated co-development across two cases**

Firm_082 appears twice as a manufacturer, again with different partners each time:

- Joint development partnership: Firm_082, Firm_072 jointly developed this construction robot [5] (census_RXM8-3).
- Joint development partnership: Firm_003, Firm_082 jointly developed this construction robot [6] (census_RXM8-1).

**Single-occurrence partnerships**

The remaining co-development cases in the provided context are one-off records with no repeated firm: census_RXM16-6 (Firm_168, Firm_054, Firm_001) and census_RXM23-5, a larger seven-firm consortium (Firm_177, Firm_002, Firm_018, Firm_068, Firm_094, Firm_134, Firm_209). None of the firms in these two records reappear elsewhere in the supplied cases.

**What to watch**

The evidence here is limited to co-occurrence in "hasManufacturer" edges within census records; it shows which firms jointly appear on a deployed process record, not a causal or capability-enabling relationship between the firms themselves. If you need to know what capability or technology readiness level these repeated partnerships achieved, that detail isn't tied to the specific co-development firm lists in this context; the profile records (e.g., RP24, census_RXM11-4) describe process characteristics separately and aren't linked here to the Firm_060 or Firm_082 co-development cases.
